outcome: Retained shader specialization that removes antialiasing edge evaluation for inactive cloud layers. No contributing layer arithmetic, filtering, precision, resolution, or cadence changed.

implementation.specialization: Compile only the launch configuration mask when fewer than two layers are enabled. The ordinary and stable full shaders remain available. The default two-layer configuration creates no additional pipelines.
implementation.selection: At cache refresh, inspect the current frame buffer. Use the specialization only when every active layer is included in its compiled mask; otherwise use the full shader. A later weather-setting change remains correct without recompilation, although a newly optimal specialization is not generated by this change.
implementation.metadata: specializedSkyAAMask is the compiled mask. skyAAMask identifies the shader used for the last visible-sky cache update.
implementation.reference: pruneCloudAA=0 always uses the full shader.
implementation.verificationOverride: testCloudAAMask forces a compiled mask only in --verify mode to test compatibility fallback.

interpretation: Clear-sky mean GPU time improves by 3.39% and p95 by 14.24%; stable-time clear skies improve by 3.34% and 13.24%. Single-layer mean improvements are 1.79–2.39% across the initial/stable comparisons. Default two-layer GPU times are effectively unchanged. Median differences are small because the visible sky refreshes at a lower cadence. No general CPU or energy benefit is claimed.

validation.fullSuite: zsh macos/test.sh completed with thirteen PASS gates; log: macos/build/inactive-cloud-aa-validation.log

rejectedDirectEdgeReuse.decision: No adoption or benchmark: stable-time output changed when sharing precomputed edge values with density evaluation. The retained specialization leaves contributing edge evaluations separate.

testTooling: verify_clouds can remove successful generated captures with --cleanup while retaining failures, records reference and selected-mask diagnostics, uses float32 thresholds for expectations, and deletes old result JSON before each run. The benchmark driver accepts finite float32 clouds/veil inputs and uses distinct weather-specific result directories.
limitations: One Apple M1; software viewport checks do not establish every physical monitor or GPU generation.
Measured steady-state timings exclude shader compilation. An inactive-layer launch compiles two additional sky variants; default two-layer launches do not.
All current/compiled mask combinations and selected scene/time/viewport states were tested; this does not prove every possible scalar setting.
Live weather input and new-specialization generation on weather transitions remain future work. The full shader fallback preserves correctness.
No power or memory-bandwidth measurements were taken.
nextCandidates: Investigate bounded saturation of cloud shadow-density FBM while preserving antialiasing edge evaluations and coordinate recurrence. Avoid sharing differently compiled edge evaluations unless all clock variants match.
